title: Lateral handoff + path MTU quirks — field notes and actions
content:
Purpose:
Quick field standup + troubleshooting journal for the Acme Health (on-prem) handoff where we saw intermittent control-plane stalls and long tail response times during model warm starts. Goal: capture observable symptoms, fast repro steps, immediate mitigations, and clear owners for the week.

Context / background:
- Customer environment: Acme Health datacenter (us-east-2 colocation). Private deployment with VPC peering to Redwood control plane; on-prem nodes run our private runtime (v1.9.3) inside k8s (kubelet 1.26).
- Recent change: rolling upgrade of node image (runtime v1.9.3 -> v1.10.0rc) + CNI tweak (calico v3.23 -> v3.24) applied by customer last week. Handoff began 2026-03-09.
- Symptom summary: occasional, reproducible 10–30s stalls on initial token generation for new chat sessions. Not full outage — control plane remains reachable, but node-level GRPC streams briefly stall then recover. Packet captures show repeated MTU blackholes on some paths.

Today’s sync (2026-03-11):
- Attendees: Maya, Omar, Jules, Anika, customer network engineer (Carlos).
- Quick timeline: reproduced stall after 3 cold starts; correlated to large SYN/ACK+TCP options size on path through customer edge switch.
- Evidence: tcpdump from node-7-srv included MSS negotiation followed by DF=1 drops when intermediate device attempted fragmentation. Traceroutes show asymmetry: control traffic -> internet egress takes different path than data path.

Observations (raw):
- Node-level: kernel tx queue backlog spikes for process redwood-runtime-worker; kernel counters show several 'frag_needed' ICMPs for >1500 byte packet.
- CNI/capture: Calico overlay MTU set to 1400 on some nodes and 1500 on others due to mixed config during the upgrade.
- Edge device: older Juniper box had a hard PMTU of 1400 on one L3 link, but didn't send consistent ICMP unreachable messages; behaviour depends on jumbo/Ethernet settings on the transit link.
- Application: redis KV cache ops unaffected, but initial KV fetch for large KV payloads (~2.5KB) triggers larger TCP segments and stalls.

Hypothesis:
1) Mixed MTU/CNI mismatch + asymmetric routing results in DF=1 packets being dropped silently by some network devices (no ICMP path MTU reported), leading to TCP stalls when runtime sends larger packets (initial KV prefetch, big model params).
2) Calico upgrade left inconsistent Felix config on some nodes (felix.confmtu mismatch) causing encapsulated packets to exceed path MTU.

Repro steps (fast):
1) From node-7-srv (customer): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap host <control-plane-ip> and trigger a new chat cold start.
2) On runtime host: sudo ip link show; sudo cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_no_pmtu_disc; sudo sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing.
3) Trigger traceroute with large packets: sudo tracepath -n <control-plane-ip> or mtr --tcp -s 2000 <control-plane-ip>.
4) Reproduce: curl to the node health endpoint while starting a generation to correlate timestamps.

Quick mitigations tried (results):
- On node (hotfix): set sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 -> immediate reduction in stalls (trial window 30m).
- On runtime side: temporarily lower socket send buffer and force smaller segment sizes at app layer (runtime flag --tcp-seg-max=1200) -> reduced incidence but requires code build + restart (deployed to canary pool).
- Customer change: forced MTU to 1400 across borderline nodes (manual) -> resolved on those nodes.

Open actions (owners + ETA):
1) Inventory nodes for MTU/cni mismatch and standardize to MTU=1400 across cluster (Owner: Carlos / customer network; Support: Omar). ETA: 2026-03-13.
2) Add runtime fallback for aggressive MTU probing: make net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 a recommended preflight check (Owner: Jules). ETA: PR 2 days.
3) Create a small runtime config flag for safe-seg-size (--max-seg-bytes) and ship to canary (Owner: Maya + eng-serving-runtime). ETA: canary by 2026-03-15.
4) Replace problematic Juniper transit link or enable proper ICMP PMTU responses (Customer + their colo vendor). Escalation ticket created (RDW-4123). Owner: Customer + SRE liaison Anika. ETA: customer timeline.
5) Automated check in install script: run tracepath and fail preflight with clear guidance if path MTU < 1400 or if PMTU discovery disabled (Owner: deploy-scripts team; PR: #78). ETA: 2026-03-18.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: If customer cannot change transit equipment quickly, we'll see intermittent stalls leading to poor tail-latency for some workloads. Mitigation: apply runtime-safe-seg default in canary and roll to Dedicated nodes as a stop-gap.
- Risk: Hardcoding MTU in doc may not fit all customers (e.g., pure on-prem with jumbo frames). Mitigation: make preflight and recommended values configurable and documented in Private Deploy runbook.

Notes to handoff (for followups):
- Capture: keep the tcpdump from node-7-srv (stored at /mnt/support/captures/acme-03-11-node-7.pcap).
- If stalls reappear after canary deploy, escalate to kernel team: suspect TCP stack corner-case with segmented GSO + VXLAN + certain NIC offloads.
- Add quick checklist item for field team: "check sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing and calico Felix MTU parity".

Meeting cadence + next check-in:
- Daily 09:30 field handoff standup for this customer until RDW-4123 closed.
- Deep dive with kernel/serving-runtime scheduled 2026-03-14 11:00 (Maya to host).

Unresolved questions / things to verify:
- Does the runtime's current batching behavior amplify MTU sensitivity (larger token batches -> larger initial payloads)? (Action: Jules to run synthetic with batch-size sweep).
- Are there NIC offload settings (GSO/TSO) that we should explicitly set in the install playbook to avoid mid-path fragmentation? (Action: Omar to validate with customer NIC vendor).

Appendix (commands observed during debug):
- ip link show
- sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
- sudo tracepath -n <control-plane-ip>
- sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 tcp port 50051 and host <control-plane-ip> -w /tmp/rdw-grpc.pcap

End notes:
This felt like a networking-first root cause with a straightforward temporary mitigation (enable tcp_mtu_probing or standardize MTU). Still, we need to bake the checks into preflight and runtime defaults to avoid recurring handoffs that rely on fragile transit devices. Please review open actions and own any followups you can move forward on.

-- Maya T.
